title: The Collapsing Family Tree
hook: Pick any total stranger on Earth — how far back until your family trees collide?
script: Pick any total stranger on Earth — how far back until your family trees collide? Doubling your ancestors every generation requires over a billion slots nine centuries ago. Yet Earth's entire population back then was only three hundred fifty million. To fit, the exact same individuals had to repeat millions of times on your tree. Go back a few thousand years, and every surviving person is an ancestor of everyone. Every human alive today, across every background, is at least a distant cousin. You inherit no DNA from most of them, but they remain your shared ancestors.

captions: How far back do you think you share a family tree with a random stranger? The math of shared ancestors is closer than you think.
Did you know every human alive today shares the exact same ancestors from just a few thousand years ago? Yes or no?
Pedigree collapse proves we are all distant cousins on one recent tree.
